stops.name: Nose
stops.blurb: Air enters here, warmed and cleaned.

pathways.title: The oxygen route
pathways.subtitle: One breath, nose to cell
pathways.intro: You just took a breath. Guide the fresh air from the nose to a hungry cell.

steps.explanation: Air enters through the nose, where tiny hairs and warm mucus clean it and warm it up.
Air slides down the windpipe — rings of cartilage keep the tube open.
In the lungs, oxygen hops across spongy walls into the blood, and carbon dioxide hops out.
The fresh, oxygen-rich blood returns to the heart, ready for a big push.
The heart pumps the blood through arteries to every cell — oxygen is handed over and work begins.

pathways.recap: Air in, oxygen across, blood carries, heart pushes, cells burn fuel. One breath's journey — repeated about 20,000 times a day.

pathways.title: The food route
pathways.subtitle: One bite, plate to cell
pathways.intro: Breakfast time. Steer each bite from the mouth all the way to the bloodstream.

steps.explanation: Teeth grind the bite into mush and saliva starts turning starch into sugar.
The tongue pushes the mush into a swallowing wave — eight seconds to the stomach.
Acid and churning squeeze the food until it becomes a soup called chyme.
Enzymes finish the job, and nutrients slip through millions of villi into the blood.
Nutrient-rich blood heads straight to the liver, which sorts, stores and releases.
The liver ships the sorted fuel on — cells everywhere take what they need for energy and repair.

pathways.recap: Grind, squeeze, churn, absorb, sort, deliver. A bite's trip from plate to cell.

pathways.title: The blood loop
pathways.subtitle: One drop, double circuit
pathways.intro: Follow one drop of blood around its double loop — the lung loop first, then the body loop.

steps.explanation: Start at the right side of the heart — this blood is dark and loaded with carbon dioxide.
The right pump sends it to the lungs, where it drops off carbon dioxide and grabs oxygen.
Bright red now, the blood returns to the left side of the heart.
The left pump pushes it out through arteries to the whole body — brain, muscles, skin.
Cells trade oxygen for carbon dioxide, and the blood flows home through veins — back to the right side. The loop begins again.

pathways.recap: Two loops, one pump pair: out to the lungs for oxygen, out to the body to spend it. Nonstop, for a lifetime.
